question: Compare the average and median price_usd in the product prices dataset, then explain why they differ.
answer: The mean and median in the product prices dataset differ because the prices are likely right-skewed, with a few very high values pulling the mean upward. [S5] The median is more representative of the typical price, as it is not affected by these outliers [S5] [S3].

citations.title: Statistics Robust Summaries
citations.text:
The mean is the sum of the values divided by their count, so every value, including extreme ones,
pulls it. The median is the middle value of the sorted data and ignores how far the extremes lie.
When a distribution is right-skewed (a long tail of a few very large values, as with prices or
incomes) a few large values drag the mean upward while the median stays near the typical value, so
the mean exceeds the median. When the data are symmetric the two are close. A large gap between the
mean and the median is therefore a quick diagnostic for skew or outliers. For skewed data, report
the median (or both) because it better describes a typical observation.

S1.title: Python Exercise Guide
S1.text:
Exercise Set B: Functions and Collections
Exercise B1. Write a function average(numbers) that returns the arithmetic mean of a list. Handle an empty list by returning None instead of dividing by zero.
Exercise B2. Count word frequency. Given a sentence, build a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to its count. Use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1. Alternative: collections.Counter.
Exercise B3. Remove duplicates from a list while preserving order. Converting to a set removes duplicates but loses ordering; use a seen set and an output list, or dict.fromkeys(items).
Exercise B4. Explain why the following function is buggy: def add_item(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items. Answer: the default list is created once and shared between calls, so items accumulate across calls. The fix is to use None as the default.

S2.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
S2.text:
4. Regression to the Mean and Effect Size
Regression to the mean is the tendency of an extreme observation to be followed by a less
extreme one when the two measurements are not perfectly correlated. A student with an unusually
high first test score will on average score lower on the second test. The name has nothing to do
with fitting a regression model.
Cohen's d measures effect size as the difference between two group means divided by the pooled
standard deviation. Conventional labels are 0.2 for a small effect, 0.5 for a medium effect and 0.8
for a large effect. Unlike a p-value, an effect size does not grow just because the sample is larger.

S4.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S4.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR.
